tier_reason: C to D: no valid measurement. Both interpreters stop at the first HALT (about 7 opcodes per timed call), the bytecode is seeded from std::random_device so the book's executed prefix is unknown and could be a single HALT, and part of the gap is the switch's range check that computed goto drops; the relayed 1.29x has no defined workload.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Directional only. The book's sample run (relayed via seed lead, not on a repo page) shows about 1.41 ns versus 1.82 ns per call, about 1.29x (derived from the relayed numbers), but the timed workload is an unknown, run-dependent prefix of about 7 opcodes, so the figure measures call overhead and a missing bounds check as much as dispatch.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: std::random_device seeding means the book's run cannot be reproduced; two runs of the same binary can differ by more than the switch-versus-goto gap. The relayed timings are a few clock cycles, so call overhead and the switch's range check weigh as much as dispatch itself; computed goto drops that check, so a bad opcode jumps out of the table (undefined behaviour). The target is skipped on MSVC. To measure dispatch, build a long HALT-free stream and validate opcodes at load time.
